_doc: Language-neutral conformance fixture for the stratified Roll estimator. The Rust synthetic harness and the Python archive analysis implement this estimator separately, so 'the same estimator applied to both corpora' would otherwise rest on two implementations happening to agree. Running this fixture through both turns that into a tested contract. Keep the implementations separate; keep this fixture shared.

units.change_vol: one value per CHANGE, already the volatility known before that change

rules.pair_assignment: a pair spans changes[i] and changes[i+1] and is assigned by change_vol[i+1], the LATER of its two changes
rules.covariance: mean over pairs of (a - mean_a)*(b - mean_b), where mean_a is the mean of first elements and mean_b the mean of second elements
rules.availability: roll_ticks is present only when covariance < 0; a non-negative covariance is UNAVAILABLE, never zero
rules.fail_closed: fewer than min_pairs covariance pairs reports fail_closed and no covariance

cases.name: negative_covariance_single_stratum
cases.why: clean alternating bounce; the estimator's intended case

cases.name: positive_covariance_unavailable
cases.why: trending runs give positive covariance; Roll has no value, and zero is not the answer

cases.name: zero_covariance_unavailable
cases.why: constant drift gives exactly zero covariance; the boundary case of the availability rule

cases.name: insufficient_pairs_fail_closed
cases.why: one pair against a minimum of three; must refuse rather than print an unstable estimate

cases.name: later_observation_assigns_stratum_low
cases.why: assigning by the EARLIER change would put two pairs here instead of one; the counts differ, so the rule is testable

cases.name: later_observation_assigns_stratum_high
cases.why: the complement of the case above; assigning by the earlier change would leave one pair here instead of two
